questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

I left my village so then I could earn more money in the city.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'so then'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect. 
 
• Here, **'so that'** should be used instead of **'so then'. **
 
• We use **“so + that”** as a **conjunction** to introduce clauses of reason and explanation. We can say that it is used to explain why an action is done.
 
• The clause after **“so that”** generally includes a modal **(like can, could, may, might, will, or would ).**
 
 
• *Example: We left a message with her secretary **so that** she would know we have come.*
 
 
 
• Here, in the given question** 'so...that' **is used to explain why the person wants to go to the city. 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is **Option 4. **

 ​

**Correct Sentence:__** *I left my village **so that** I could earn more money in the city. * 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__**

__
 
• दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरणिक रूप से गलत है।
 
• यहाँ, 'so then' कि जगह 'so that’ का प्रयोग करना चाहिए।
 
• हम कारण और स्पष्टीकरण के खंडों को पेश करने के लिए एक संयोजन के रूप में "so + that" का उपयोग करते हैं। हम कह सकते हैं कि इसका उपयोग यह समझाने के लिए किया जाता है कि कार्रवाई क्यों की जाती है।
 
• “so + that” के बाद के खंड में आम तौर पर एक मोडल शामिल होता है (जैसे, can, could, may, might, will, or would ))।
 
 
• *Example: We left a message with her secretary so that she would know we have come.*
 
 
 
• यहाँ, दिए गए प्रश्न में so ... that ’ का उपयोग यह बताने के लिए किया जाता है कि व्यक्ति शहर क्यों जाना चाहता है।
 
• इसलिए, ऊपर वर्णित बिंदुओं के अनुसार, हम पाते हैं कि सही उत्तर Option 4 है।

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error. **

Many prince and nobleman wished to marry the beautiful princess.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Many prince and nobleman'. **

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect. 
 
• Here, **'Many princes and noblemen'** should be used instead of **'Many prince and nobleman'. **
 
• We use many to refer to a large number of something countable. 
 
• The quantifier **'many'** is **plural**. Hence, in the given question plural nouns that are **'princes and noblemen'** will be used. 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is **Option 3. **

 ​

**Correct Sentence:__** ***Many princes and noblemen** wished to marry the beautiful princess. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Let's have a look at different usage of the quantifier **'Many':**

 
 

 **Usage**
 **Example**
 
 

 We don’t normally use **many** alone before a noun in an affirmative statement
 
 
There were a lot of people at the swimming pool this morning.****

 
There were many people at the swimming pool this morning.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b91b169c9a6aba309887b5e1410c56688829831001bc1448ed23f1bec5eca1d8.png] *

 
 
 

 We often use **many** in 'formal situations' in affirmative statements when the noun is followed by a relative clause (acting as a postmodifier)
 *There are **many** elderly people who have never touched a computer in their lives.*
 
 

 We can use the expression **as many as** to talk about a high number that is surprising or shocking
 ***As many as** 5,000 people are believed to have died in the earthquake.*

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

Some tigers are smuggled about the country as exotic pets.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'about the country'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect. 
 
• Here,** 'out of the country'** should be used instead of **'about the country'.**
 
• The phrase **'out of the country'** means 'an outlying area or country'.
 
• Here, exotic pets mean **'wild animal or one that's more unusual than your standard dog or cat'. **
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is **Option 4. **

 ​

**Correct Sentence:__** *Some tigers are smuggled **out of the country **as exotic pets.*

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

If I want to gave you some advice, would you be interested?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'gave you some advice'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect. 
 
• Here,** 'give you some advice'** should be used instead of **'gave you some advice'. **
 
• We know that the **base** form of verb is always used with the** to-infinitive.** 
 
 
• *Example: *
 
 
• *Jennifer wants to **improve** her skills. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/69a779acc017790d2eea790cc9122762921b180090c4a6901b9133fe30db56bd.png] *
 
• *Jennifer wants to **improved** her skills. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b91b169c9a6aba309887b5e1410c56688829831001bc1448ed23f1bec5eca1d8.png] *
 
 
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is **Option 1. **

 ​

**Correct Sentence:__** *If I want to give you some advice, would you be interested?* 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__*** *

 
• The verbs/adjectives/phrases given below are followed by 'V1 + ing':

 
 
• with a view to, addicted to, given/taken to, prone to, in addition to, look forward to, owing to, etc.
 
 
 
• ​For example:
 
 
• *​Radhika looks forward to have a great time with you. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b91b169c9a6aba309887b5e1410c56688829831001bc1448ed23f1bec5eca1d8.png] *
 
• *Radhika looks forward to having a great time with you. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/69a779acc017790d2eea790cc9122762921b180090c4a6901b9133fe30db56bd.png] *

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

Instead of watching television or playing video games, children should be encouraged reading books.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** ****reading books.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **T****o**-infinitive is the 'to + the base form of the verb', e.g., to sing, to dance, etc.
 
• There are certain verbs that are used in a particular pattern given below:
 
 
• Subject + verb + noun/pronoun + to-infinitive.
 
 
 
• Some of the verbs are given below:
 
 
• ask, tell, advise, encourage, urge, wish, intend, invite, help, allow, hate, permit, etc.
 
 
 
• For example:
 
 
• *​I urge you helping me solve this problem. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b91b169c9a6aba309887b5e1410c56688829831001bc1448ed23f1bec5eca1d8.png] *
 
• *​I urge you to help me solve this problem. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/69a779acc017790d2eea790cc9122762921b180090c4a6901b9133fe30db56bd.png] *
 
 
 
• According to the rule and the example given above, 'to read' will be used instead of '**reading**' in the part given in the **1st option.**

 

Correct Sentence__:* **Instead of watching television or playing video games, children should be encouraged **to read **books.*

*​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__***

 
• There are certain verbs that are used in a particular pattern given below:
 
 
• Subject + verb + present participle(-ing form of verb)
 
 
 
• Some of the verbs are given below:
 
 
• hate, stop, finish, enjoy, prefer, keep, rest, worth, propose, regret, etc.
 
 
 
• ​Example:
 
 
• *He hates working out early in the morning.*

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

Due to heavy rain, the bridge collapsed leads to a huge traffic jam.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is- leads to​.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The simple past tense is used to talk about things that happened or existed before now.
 
• It shows that we are talking about something that has already happened. 
 
• The structure is given below:
 
 
• Subject + V2 + object.
 
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *​Wolfgang entered a hula hoop contest.*
 
 
 
• As per the given sentence, the instance of collapsing of the bridge took place and this led to a huge traffic jam.
 
• Hence according to the rule and example given above, 'which led' will be used instead of '**leads**' in the part given in the** 3rd option.**

 

​Correct Sentence__: *Due to heavy rain, the bridge collapsed **which led to **a huge traffic jam.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__***

 
• Some phrases are followed by past indefinite/simple tense as given below:

 
 
• ​It's high time, It's time, It's about time, etc.
 
 
 
• For example:
 
 
• It's high time I start preparing for my final exams*.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b91b169c9a6aba309887b5e1410c56688829831001bc1448ed23f1bec5eca1d8.png]

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

Nobody is allowed to entered the colony during the lockdown.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'to entered'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A verb is a word that denotes an action or a state.
 
• An infinitive is a non-finite verb that doesn't change according to the subject or tense.
 
 
• It follows the structure: to + base form of the verb.
 
• Example: I like to write in English.
 
• Example: He went to the market to buy some flowers.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, 'to' is the part of the infinitive, so it must take the base form of the verb.
 
• Thus, 'to entered' should be replaced with 'to enter' to make the sentence correct.

Correct sentence__: *Nobody is allowed to enter the colony during the lockdown.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__***

 
• Infinitive as Noun: 

 
 
• ​Example:* *To travel is the only thing on her mind.

questions.question:
Directions: Each item in this section has a sentence with three underlined parts labelled as (a), (b) and (c). Read each sentence to find out whether there is any error in any underlined part and indicate your response on the answer sheet against the corresponding letter, i.e., (a) or (b) or (c). If you find no error, your response should be indicated as (d).

__They had to wait for the luggages__ (a)/ __to be put into the cab__ (b)/ __before they themselves got into it__(c)/ __No error__(d).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is* "***They had to wait for ****for the luggage​".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There are some uncountable nouns (followed by a singular verb) which don't take the articles 'a/an', many, few, and plural forms:​

 
 
• Furniture, scenery, luggage, temper, hair, knowledge, equipment, pottery, music, jewellery, etc.​
 
• Example:
 
 
• *​The sceneries at my friend's house enchanted me. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b91b169c9a6aba309887b5e1410c56688829831001bc1448ed23f1bec5eca1d8.png] *
 
• *The scenery at my friend's house enchanted me. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/69a779acc017790d2eea790cc9122762921b180090c4a6901b9133fe30db56bd.png] *
 
 
 
 
 
• As per the rule given above, 'luggage' will be used instead of 'luggages' in the 4th **part **of the given question.

 

Correct sentence__: *They had to wait for the **luggage **to be put into the cab before they themselves got into it.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__***

__
 
• The nouns given below seem plural in form but in actuality are singular:

 
 
• ​news, billiards, summons, physics, measles, innings, etc.
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *​Physics is an interesting subject.​*
 
 
 
 
 
• हाँ कुछ uncountable nouns (followed by a singular verb) जो article 'a/an', many, few, and plural form: नहीं लेते हैं:
 
 
• Furniture, scenery, luggage, temper, hair, knowledge, equipment, pottery, music, jewellery, etc.​
 
• उदाहरण :
 
 
• *The sceneries at my friend's house enchanted me. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b91b169c9a6aba309887b5e1410c56688829831001bc1448ed23f1bec5eca1d8.png] *
 
• *The scenery at my friend's house enchanted me. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/69a779acc017790d2eea790cc9122762921b180090c4a6901b9133fe30db56bd.png] *
 
 
 
 
 
• ऊपर दिए गए नियम के अनुसार, 'luggage' को देखते हुए सवाल के 4th part में 'luggages' के स्थान पर इस्तेमाल किया जाएगा।

 

सही वाक्य__: *They had to wait for the luggage to be put into the cab before they themselves got into it.*
